Their 2026 paper compares the domination number, the smallest vertex set whose closed neighborhoods cover every vertex, with the packing number, the largest set whose closed neighborhoods stay disjoint. The question is which graph families keep their ratio bounded by a constant.

The main result improves the upper bound on that ratio for planar graphs. The team also extends the bounded-ratio list to chordal bipartite graphs and homogeneously orderable graphs, and gives a simple direct proof for trees. The work tightens a classic comparison between covering and packing in graphs, with new families where the two numbers stay within a constant factor of each other.
arxiv-2602-18502:
Sarah Müller and Philipp Berens benchmark a fix for shortcuts in medical imaging. Their 2026 paper notes deep learning models in medical imaging often classify well yet rely on shortcuts, exploiting spurious correlations or confounders unrelated to the target task. That poses risks in clinics, where models must generalize across hospitals and scanners.

Feature disentanglement cuts shortcuts by separating task info from confounder features in latent representations. The study tests disentanglement methods, including adversarial learning and latent splitting by dependence control, across one artificial dataset and two medical sets with natural and synthetic confounders. Mitigation methods improved classification under strong spurious links in training, while latent studies revealed representation gaps missed by classification metrics. Reliance on shortcuts depended on training-data confounding. The best models combine data rebalancing with model disentanglement, achieving stronger, more robust mitigation than rebalancing alone at similar cost.
arxiv-2602-18602:
Ryan Gibb and four co-authors unify package tools across languages and systems. Their 2026 paper notes package tools are legion: every language and operating system offers its own tool, each with different semantics for resolving dependencies. This fragmentation blocks precise multilingual work, leaves external needs implicit, and obscures the graph for supply-chain analysis.

The team presents the Package Calculus, a formalism for core rules. They show this core covers diverse real-world languages for expressing needs. The calculus provides the basis for future cross-ecosystem tools, a shared language for expressing needs.
arxiv-2602-18802:
At a cocktail party, recognising emotion means first pulling one voice out of a noisy mix. Multi-channel audio should help with that job, but it is rarely tested end to end. Youjun Chen, with eleven co-authors, shows in 2026 that a multi-channel speech enhancement front end materially improves speech emotion recognition in such settings.

A dereverberation and separation front end combining DNN-WPE with mask-based MVDR extracts the target speaker. A back end built on HuBERT and vision transformer features then judges emotion. On mixtures built from IEMOCAP and MSP-FACE data, the enhanced input beats fine-tuned single-channel baselines by clear margins in accuracy and F1 score. A front end trained on one dataset still generalises zero-shot to the other, which matters for real rooms.
arxiv-2602-19202:
Event cameras do not take ordinary pictures. They record only where brightness changes, which makes them fast, frugal with power, and good in harsh light, but their output drops most still detail and texture. Turning that sparse stream back into watchable video is the problem Gang Xu and two colleagues take on.

Their system, UniE2F, leans on a video diffusion model that already knows how scenes should look, and uses it to rebuild full frames from event data. A first baseline feeds events straight into the model as a guide. The work then builds on the physical link between events and ordinary frames, so the rebuilt video keeps both motion and the still detail that raw event streams lose.
arxiv-2602-19502:
Agentic AI can run data science workflows on its own, yet clinical forecasting demands domain know-how that pure auto tools struggle to supply. Lalitha Pranathi Pulavarthy and five co-authors study human-guided agentic AI for multimodal clinical forecasting through the AgentDS Healthcare benchmark. Human analysts steered the workflow at key choice points across three tasks.

The tasks cover 30-day hospital readmission risk, emergency department cost forecasting, and discharge readiness checks, with strong scores on each. Guidance shaped multimodal feature design from clinical notes, scanned billing receipts, and vital-sign time series, plus model choice and clinically guided checks. The approach ranked fifth overall in healthcare, third on discharge readiness, with knockout tests showing guided decisions piling up.
arxiv-2602-19902:
Granular materials, from soils to powders, are not the same in every direction. That direction effect has two sources that tests struggle to separate: the material's inner fabric and the direction of the stress itself. A 2026 arXiv paper by Mehdi Pouragha and three co-authors develops a first-order linearization of small stress-strain steps that isolates the two.

Using two independent orientation gauges, the setup measures the stress-driven and fabric-driven parts directly from lab-scale data. Applied to hollow-cylinder tests with varied loading directions, it shows both parts grow as stress grows more uneven. The mechanical part is consistently stronger, but relatively less dominant at higher uneven stress. A check against an isotropic hypoplastic model confirms that direction effects from stress alone are captured even without fabric effects.
arxiv-2602-20002:
Qubits built from superconductors depend on Josephson junctions, and tuning those junctions after making could fix frequency crowding in quantum chips. A 2026 arXiv paper led by Christian Križan with a large team studies electrical tuning of aluminum junctions at room temperature.

Voltage pulses raise junction resistance in a controlled way and adjust Josephson energy, while qubit quality factors stay above one million. The rate of rise grows ever faster with pulse size during handling, and it keeps rising afterward on its own, in proportion to both starting resistance and prior handling. That self-driven rise pauses at deep-cold temperatures and resumes at room temperature. A stepwise protocol reaches a large resistance increase with a matching drop in qubit transition frequency, mapping the practical limits of tuning after making.
arxiv-2602-20102:
Large language models remain open to adversarial attacks and unsafe outputs. That vulnerability blocks use in high-stakes settings. Safety fixes need both practical force and theory-based grounding. A 2026 arXiv paper by Thanh Q. Tran and five co-authors introduces BarrierSteer, a framework for safer responses at inference time.

BarrierSteer writes learned nonlinear safety constraints into the model's hidden representation space. Hidden-state safety classifiers serve as control barrier functions, steering unsafe latent paths. Multiple safety constraints combine through efficient constraint merging, without changing the base model parameters, so model utility is preserved. Theory shows the approach is sound, modular, and cheap to run. Its guarantees hold when the learned barriers capture the safety property intended. Broad tests across model kinds and datasets show BarrierSteer cuts attack success and unsafe generations sharply, beating the existing method. The code is openly available.
arxiv-2602-20402:
Young stars flare often, and those flares shape how their planets evolve. Andrew Tran and Inseok Song study flares and rotation in members of nearby young moving groups, using data from the TESS mission. Their sample covers four hundred seventeen members aged ten to one hundred fifty million years, with light curves from the first four TESS cycles.

Using detrended light curves plus extra detrending for fast rotators, the pair detects six thousand two hundred eighty-eight flares from twenty-seven thousand four hundred sixteen candidates. Every member analyzed shows at least one flare. Flaring rates fall with age for high-energy flares on late-type stars, and ten-minute cadence data yield five and a half times more flares than thirty-minute data. Extreme-energy events on M-dwarf and Sun-like stars carry implications for exoplanet habitability.
arxiv-2602-21002:
Little Red Dots are massive, compact galaxies in the early universe whose rapid growth strains formation models. M. Liempi and six co-authors test how their black holes could have formed in this 2026 arXiv paper, using X-ray non-detections to constrain collision-based formation scenarios. The galaxies look like ideal birthplaces for massive black holes, yet many show no strong active-nucleus X-ray emission.

Collision models predict seed masses larger than local ones, and consistency with stacked X-ray limits requires particular accretion and obscuration parameters. Constant or rising star formation with high Eddington ratios can work only with heavy obscuration or enrichment, while moderate sub-Eddington accretion reconciles massive seeds with X-ray weakness. The authors conclude these galaxies should eventually evolve into active nuclei.
arxiv-2602-21102:
Resettable smart sheets promise tunable radio channels, but workers need read data to model them. Mattia Piana, Giovanni Alghisi, Anna Guglielmi, Giovanni Perin, Francesco Gringoli, and Stefano Tomasin present such a set in this 2026 arXiv paper. BRISC holds channel readings at about five and a half gigahertz with a mirror smart sheet. Two software-defined radios, in step by a shared clock, serve as sender and listener.

Sheet parts are grouped into blocks sharing one binary state, and channel data span sender spots, grouping grain sizes, and sheet setups. About ten thousand setups per sender spot were tried. The authors also tune leading channel models to the readings, making BRISC a robust yardstick for link work.
arxiv-2602-21202:
Late-interaction retrieval matches queries against many document vectors, but storage and compute grow with document length. Hanxiang Qin, Alexander Martin, Rohan Jha, Chunsheng Zuo, Reno Kriz, and Benjamin Van Durme compress those representations in this 2026 arXiv paper, under a fixed vector budget. Four query-agnostic methods are compared: sequence resizing, memory tokens, hierarchical pooling, and attention-guided clustering.

Attention-guided clustering picks semantically salient regions as cluster centroids and weights token aggregation, beating other parameterized methods and offering more size flexibility than hierarchical pooling. Across text, visual-document, and video retrieval tasks, it matches or improves on a full uncompressed index. The work makes late interaction practical for image-, video-, and audio-rich collections.
arxiv-2602-21702:
Riccardo Lasagno presents the Half Pound Filter, a tweak of the 1 Euro Filter for smoothing motion data in real-time animation. When an animation switches clips, the bone path jumps, and filtering must hide the jump without visible artifacts. The paper adds data-driven tuning and a trigger based on motion derivative checks, so blending starts and ends at the right moments.

Tests on an example from the LaFAN1 dataset compare the filter with common animation filters by mean squared error and a spectrum similarity measure. The Half Pound Filter replays the motion with higher fidelity, and results are reported for both a fixed trigger point and the automatic trigger and recovery system.
arxiv-2602-21802:
Aimeric Malter and one co-author study toric non-commutative crepant resolutions for algebras tied to a rational convex polyhedral Gorenstein cone over a lattice polytope. They show that toric resolutions of the cone's algebra descend to those tied to faces of the shape.

Hence, the paper gives two new, short proofs that toric resolutions exist for simplicial affine toric Gorenstein cases and for almost simplicial ones. Those are tied to cones with one more edge ray than the size. The descent argument thus turns a result about one cone into results about all its faces, shortening the path to existence in the simplicial and almost simplicial cases.
arxiv-2602-21902:
Vu Tung Lam Dinh and Ivan Chi-Ho Ip present a 2026 mathematics paper on cluster varieties built from surfaces. Cluster algebras track how variables change under set swaps called mutations. The space here encodes twisted local systems on a surface, a rich object in geometry.

The authors derive general recurrence rules for cluster variables when a triangulation flips. Their method rests on detailed counting for a standard polygon cut into small triangles. They work the first two cases fully and also treat the non-simply-laced G2 type. They prove a well-triangulated property for mutations under flips. They also count the monomials in the expansion formula. The result is a combinatorial frame for how these structures stay stable.
arxiv-2602-22002:
Seventy years ago, John Marstrand published a paper linking the size of a flat set, measured by Hausdorff dimension, to the sizes of its shadows cast onto lines. Kenneth J. Falconer surveys the long afterlife of that paper, which drew little notice at first. Over the past forty years, Marstrand's projection theorems have grown into the prototype for a whole field of results in fractal geometry.

Falconer traces the many variants and uses that followed, showing how one idea about shadows seeded questions that still drive leading research. The survey suits readers who want the story of a slow-burning classic: a quiet paper that became a standard tool. It also shows how fractal geometry keeps returning to Marstrand's simple question about what a shadow can reveal.
arxiv-2602-22102:
City quantum networks must carry secret keys across mixed channels, from open air to buried fiber, without losing sync. Karolina Dziwulska and five co-authors demonstrate high-dimensional time-bin quantum key distribution over a hybrid city link that mixes free-space transmission with fiber. They run both two- and four-level protocols at a fast clock rate in the telecom band.

The headline feat is endurance: the system ran continuously for two days in a fully self-referenced design, with sync, phase stability, and drift correction drawn only from the quantum signals themselves. No helper optical channels were needed. Secure key rates held up under substantial loss, making the platform a practical step toward city-scale quantum networks.
arxiv-2602-22402:
Long reasoning sessions in language models accumulate valuable state: design maps, trade-off decisions, codebase conventions. Cosmo Santoni notes that state vanishes when sessions hit context limits and undergo lossy compaction. He proposes Contextual Memory Virtualisation, treating that stored know-how as versioned state, borrowing virtual-memory ideas from OS design.

Session history becomes a directed acyclic graph with defined snapshot, branch, and trim operations for context reuse across parallel sessions. A three-pass trimming algorithm preserves every user and assistant message verbatim while cutting tokens by a fifth on average, and far more for bloated sessions, by stripping tool outputs, images, and metadata. A single-user case study evaluates the design.
arxiv-2602-23002:
V. Ayyar and thirteen co-authors compute the gravity-wave signal of a lock-in transition in Hyper Stealth Dark Matter. The low-energy sector is a one-flavour SU(4) gauge theory with a single flavour of basic quarks, studied on the lattice with moving fermion runs as a true-to-life, strongly linked dark matter model.

The team works out the gravity-wave spectrum from the first-order lock-in transition in the early cosmos. Dark sea quarks lower the boundary tension in the working potential of the Polyakov loop. The runs show this effect numerically lowers the gravity-wave amplitude, a concrete prediction linking a stealth dark sector to an observable cosmological signal.
arxiv-2602-23102:
John Southworth presents TEPCat, the Transiting Extrasolar Planet Catalogue. Passing far planets are hugely valuable for studying planet traits and birth, since they are the only far planets whose bodily and orbital traits can be gauged well. Thousands are now known, making a kept-up database essential for the scientific community.

TEPCat performs this task as a key collection of the bodily and visible traits of known passing planetary systems. The work presents the reasons, scope, contents, and build of the catalogue, builds plots of interesting numbers, and discusses the sorting of planets and of shadow features in their light curves. TEPCat is kept up and openly online.
arxiv-2602-23802:
Yiyang Fang and seven co-authors present EMO-R3, a training framework that aims to improve emotional reasoning in multimodal language models. The 2026 paper argues that such models still struggle with the complexity and subjectivity of human emotion, and that plain fine-tuning gives limited generalization and weak explanations.

EMO-R3 guides models through structured, step-by-step emotional thinking, so each judgment can be traced. A reflective reward then asks the model to re-check its reasoning against visual-text consistency and emotional coherence. Tests across several visual emotion benchmarks show clear gains in both interpretability and emotional understanding over prior methods. The framework offers a route to models whose emotional calls are easier to audit and trust.
arxiv-2602-24102:
Kai-Xuan Wen and three co-authors estimate the performance boundary between two bosonic quantum error-correcting codes, Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill codes and number-phase codes, which encode logical information in a harmonic oscillator. The 2026 paper asks under which physical noise conditions, combining photon loss and dephasing, each encoding intrinsically outperforms the other.

By optimizing code parameters within each family, the authors map the noise regimes where each code holds a fundamental advantage. The crossover occurs when dephasing strength is roughly two orders of magnitude smaller than loss strength, and operational regimes separate sharply there, so each code wins in its own noise range. The work offers an extensible methodology and gives experimenters concrete guidance for choosing and deploying bosonic encodings under realistic noise.
arxiv-2602-24202:
Alexis E. Laudenslager and three co-authors evaluate the accuracy of vine robot shape sensing with distributed inertial measurement units. The 2026 paper studies soft, tip-extending vine robots, well suited to tight, debris-filled spaces for urban search and rescue. Knowing the full body shape helps localize sensor data and determine configuration in explored spaces.

Earlier work localized vine robot tips with a single inertial unit plus force or length sensing. One method showed full-body sensing with distributed units on a passively steered robot in controlled mazes. This study systematically quantifies accuracy under active steering, varied lengths, and sensor spacings. Mean tip position error runs about a tenth of robot length for passive steering. It rises for active steering and is lower during growth experiments across lengths from short to long, with error trending up with length. Intermediate sensor spacings prove favorable, guiding design trade-offs.
arxiv-2603-00002: Matthews proves a polygon can be pinned down from section lengths alone. The sections are non-central and hold a piecewise-analytic hedgehog inside the polygon. He also proves the matching slab-area result for centrally symmetric polygons. Those shapes can be rebuilt from slab areas holding an analytic mirror-image hedgehog inside.
arxiv-2603-00102: Dogan, Markelius and Gunes argue ethical, user-adapted explainability must become a core design goal for social robots driven by foundation models. Generic explanations now cloak behaviour from models trained on vast, opaque datasets, so one-size-fits-all accounts fail users. The authors name open challenges where adaptation and explanation are both handed to foundation models. They propose four recommendations toward user-adapted, modality-aware and co-designed explanations grounded in smaller, fairer datasets, illustrated with an LLM-driven assistive robot case.
arxiv-2603-00302: Damera and colleagues extend differentiable logic gate networks to ternary Kleene logic, where an UNKNOWN state lets a circuit abstain under uncertainty. The established approach breaks down because each neuron could take nearly twenty thousand possible gates. Their Polynomial Surrogate Training instead writes each ternary neuron as a degree-two polynomial with nine coefficients, and proves the gap to the discrete circuit vanishes at convergence. Ternary networks train two to three times faster than binary ones, and UNKNOWN outputs serve as an uncertainty signal for selective prediction.
arxiv-2603-00602: Sun and eight colleagues improve graph out of distribution detection, where training only on in distribution graphs leaves feature space patchy and decision boundaries weak. Fixed sampling heuristics for synthetic outliers cannot explore informative regions well. Their Policy-Guided Outlier Synthesis trains a reinforcement learning agent to roam low density areas of a structured latent space and sample boundary sharpening representations. Decoding those samples into pseudo outlier graphs strengthens detectors, reaching state of the art results on graph outlier and anomaly benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-00802: Salmon and three colleagues revisit machine learning for the universal density functional of the one dimensional Hubbard model with random site potentials. Exact diagonalisation on an eight site closed chain supplies ground state data, and component analysis reveals low dimensional structure in the joint density potential space. An energy filter narrows data near weakly perturbed zero values, and a compact convolutional net with lattice symmetry tricks learns the functional to near exact accuracy. The team also notes a subtlety: good functional values need not imply good functional derivatives.
arxiv-2603-00902: Dong, Feng, and Wang expose a token-drain attack on OpenClaw, an open-source self-hosted assistant with a community skill ecosystem. Their trojanized skill steers the agent through a staged verification protocol via injected instructions and a helper script. Token use grows six to seven times over a benign baseline, near nine times in a costly failure setup. The agent sometimes routes around brittle steps with general tools, softening the drain, and the authors map further production attack routes.
arxiv-2603-01302: Tran and three colleagues propose Hybrid TD3, a spin-off of Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient for discrete-smooth hybrid action spaces. There, high-level task choices and low-level joint moves must be jointly tuned. They analyze over-guess bias strictly under twin-critic setups, giving formal bounds and a complete bias ranking across five method variants under synced Gaussian error rules. Building on that analysis, they offer a weighted clipped Q-learning target that averages across discrete actions, getting equal bias cut.
arxiv-2603-02002:
Yuanchang Zhou, Siyu Hu, Xiangyu Zhang, and colleagues build a fast interatomic potential that skips costly tensor math. Their 2026 model, MatRIS, predicts atomic interactions for materials screening across many chemistries. Top equivariant models are accurate but expensive, since they lean on tensor products and high-degree features.

MatRIS stays invariant instead and models three-body interactions with a separable attention mechanism. That attention scales linearly with atom count, which keeps large systems affordable. Accuracy matches leading equivariant models across a wide range of popular benchmarks in their tests. On a discovery benchmark, it reaches a strong score at lower training cost than those rivals. Careful invariant design, the authors argue, can equal equivariant accuracy at a fraction of the price.
arxiv-2603-02502:
Naoki Awaya, Keisuke Sasaki, Genya Kobayashi, and Shonosuke Sugasawa model collections of distributions in this 2026 paper. Surveys record whole distributions, like age or income mixes, across many places. Bayesian factor models can summarize such data through lower-dimensional structures. Standard mixture models struggle when distributions show no clear clusters.

A tree-based transformation first embeds each distribution into ordinary Euclidean space. A Bayesian latent factor model then works in that transformed space. The model imposes no parametric shape on the observed distributions. Spatial dependence can be added through a standard autoregressive prior. Tests on real population data beat Dirichlet mixture models and parametric rivals. The approach suits grouped social science data where common and local structures both matter.
arxiv-2603-02802:
Tianlin Pan, Jiayi Dai, Chenpu Yuan, and colleagues edit videos without needing matched before-and-after training pairs. Their 2026 framework, NOVA, splits the job into sparse control and dense synthesis. Paired editing data are scarce, above all for local edits, and older pair-free tricks often broke backgrounds or timing.

In NOVA, a user edits a few keyframes, and those frames steer the meaning of the edit across the clip. A second branch keeps pulling motion and texture from the original video, preserving fidelity and smooth flow. Training uses artificially degraded videos, teaching the model to rebuild motion and timing without real pairs. In extensive tests, NOVA beat prior methods on edit accuracy, motion preservation, and coherence over time.
arxiv-2603-02902:
Ziruo Hao, Tao Yang, Xiaofeng Wu, and Bo Hu hunt for cause-and-effect links in environmental data that stay true over time. Their 2026 framework, DisDy-ICPT, works on time series spread across sites that cannot share raw data freely. Older methods handled change over time or stable causes, but rarely both in a distributed setting.

The method learns causal links that shift with time while stripping out spatial confounders, all without moving data between sites. Theory shows it recovers stable causal predictors within a bounded number of communication rounds. On synthetic tests and real environment-split datasets, it beat baselines on stability and accuracy. The authors point to carbon monitoring and weather forecasting as natural uses.
arxiv-2603-03302:
Divija Amaram and three colleagues build an artificial intelligence assistant for state transportation departments in the United States. Agencies hold huge stores of manuals, guidelines, and research reports, while senior engineers retire and take hard-won knowledge with them. New staff face steep learning curves, and finding one right fact in the pile can take far too long.

Their 2026 system pairs document search with language model answers, split among specialized agents that retrieve, draft, evaluate, and refine queries in rounds. A vision-language model also turns technical figures into searchable text, so diagrams count as knowledge too. Tested on hundreds of real department documents with one hundred pavement questions, the system placed the right source in its top three results almost every time.
arxiv-2603-04102: Ricerchi and Crida reconsider the exposure age of Saturn's rings. At Cassini's end, the rings were claimed young versus the Solar System. Their ice-rich composition was explained as pure ice rings gradually polluted by interplanetary dust over 100 to 400 million years. The authors review exposure-age steps, asking how the age depends on settings and its relevance. They derive a new expression for planar-ring gravitational focusing and a formula for dust fraction over time. Possible impact vaporisation is included, and a space-weathering cleaning process is presented.
arxiv-2603-04202: Gunara and colleagues develop Coulomb sectors and scattering for Maxwell-Higgs fields around Schwarzschild and slowly rotating Kerr black holes. They build a small-data Maxwell-Higgs theory for the Schwarzschild and slowly rotating Kerr exteriors for gauge-invariant nonnegative self-interactions around the trivial vacuum. The Coulomb-sector analysis pins down the right long-range normalization for fixed electric sectors and separates proved results from remaining rotating massive final-state problems.
arxiv-2603-04302: Li and colleagues fix a flaw in unsupervised keypoint face animation: identity and motion stay tangled. Their MMFA method first learns expression codes apart from rotation, translation, and other motion cues. A new keypoint computation then targets arbitrary motion control, and a variational autoencoder maps expressions to a continuous Gaussian distribution. That mapping allows expression interpolation with no labels, and public dataset tests show gains in realism and motion control. Faces thus move as users direct, with looks held steady.
arxiv-2603-04402: Jerome Hsu builds SearchGym, a modular base for hybrid search benchmarks. Toolkits abound, yet prototypes rarely grow into robust production systems. SearchGym splits data, embeddings, and retrieval into Dataset, VectorSet, and App parts. A config algebra builds whole systems from layered configs with perfect reproducibility. Top-k order matters: the best mix of ranking and filtering depends on filter strength. On LitSearch it hits a 70 percent top-100 rate, showing tension between generality and optimizability.
arxiv-2603-04702: Sasa and Hattori model single-q and double-q orders in an XY model on the diamond structure, for quadrupole order in PrIr2Zn20. Quadrupole order at L points in PrIr2Zn20 under magnetic fields is analyzed with Monte Carlo simulations on a Gamma-3 quadrupole model. Competition between field and quadrupole anisotropy yields a rich phase diagram for fields parallel to [001], including switching between single-q and double-q states. A symmetry-allowed biquadratic intersite interaction, matching a hexadecapole interaction, proves crucial for weak-field topology seen in experiments.
arxiv-2603-04802: Cao defines the Archimedean height pairing for differential forms on degenerating Riemann surfaces. The forms are fiberwise cohomologically trivial, and the paper studies the pairing's asymptotic behavior. The proof uses recent work by Dai and Yoshikawa on asymptotics of small eigenvalues. As an application, the pairing relates to the current-valued pairing of Filip and Tosatti. The construction extends Filip and Tosatti's work to broader geometric settings. The result connects height pairings with current-valued pairings on degenerations.
arxiv-2603-04902: Ivoline C. Ngong and colleagues argue that privacy checks for agentic systems miss most risk by looking only at inputs and final outputs. Their Privacy Flow Graph, a Contextual Integrity framework, breaks an agent run into tagged flows so leaks can be traced to their origin. AgentSCOPE spans eight regulatory domains and 62 multi-tool scenarios, with ground truth at every stage. Testing seven leading models finds violations in over 80% of cases, mostly at the tool-response stage, even where final outputs appear clean.
arxiv-2603-05002: Rustem Islamov and team interpret the Edge of Balance through Directional Smoothness, stretching it to non-Euclidean norms. Sharpness, the Hessian's largest eigenvalue, ways and hovers near the balance threshold during gradient descent, apparently violating classical smoothness assumptions. Their carried over sharpness measure covers vanilla and preconditioned gradient descent as special cases, plus before unstudied methods such as l-infinity descent, Block CD, and Spectral GD. Tests on neural networks show non-Euclidean gradient descent also exhibits progressive sharpening followed by swing around or above the threshold.
arxiv-2603-05102: Maelys Magnier and the rest of the team present Lagrangian readings of particle dispersion in stratified turbulence from a test at high buoyancy Reynolds number and low Froude number. Stratification constrains vertical dispersion to around the buoyancy scale, vertical speed standard drift over Brunt-Väisälä rate. Above that rate the Lagrangian speed spectrum becomes isotropic, decaying as 1/f^3 rather than the 1/f^2 of homogeneous isotropic turbulence. Speed increment statistics stay Gaussian at internal-wave timescales but turn non-Gaussian at smaller scales, indicating wave-breaking-driven nonlinear dynamics.
arxiv-2603-05302: Seokhoon Moon and team offer SLICE, speech enhancement by layer-wise conditioning injection. Real speech suffers noise, reverberation, and distortion, while diffusion work struggles with compound corruptions. Noise-aware ways inject it only at input, sometimes lagging unconditioned models. SLICE injects degradation conditioning into the timestep embedding, so it propagates through residual blocks without architectural changes. It comes from a multi-task encoder. In controlled tests varying only the entry point, input-level cues lag behind no encoder on compound damage, while layer-wise entry leads on real recordings.
arxiv-2603-06302: Bousselham and his team present DEX-AR, an explainability method for autoregressive vision language models that makes per token and sequence level heatmaps of image regions behind responses. Classification work struggles with token by token generation and visual textual interactions. DEX-AR reads models by working out layer gradients over attention maps as it runs, with weight that shifts across layers and tokens. Two ideas drive it: dynamic head filtering spotting visually focused heads, and sequence filtering that gathers per token notes while sorting grounded tokens from linguistic ones.
arxiv-2603-06402: Schirneck studies transversal rank, the maximum size of a hypergraph's minimal hitting sets. Deciding transversal rank at least k for n vertices and m edges takes O(m^{k+1}n) time with a 1970s algorithm. His first result recognizes transversal rank at least k in O(Δ^{k-2}mn^{k-1}) time, with Δ the maximum degree. His look ahead method finds higher order extensions augmenting a set with at least two more vertices. He shows reducing computation to poly(m)·n^{k+O(1)} time equals breakthroughs including k-conformal recognition.
arxiv-2603-06602: Ciaperoni and team bring the Khatri-Rao clustering paradigm, stretching Centre-based grouping to produce succinct yet accurate data summaries by saying centroids arise from interactions of multiple proto-centre sets. Centre-based grouping finds briefs as few prototypes per cluster, yet briefs often contain repeats, limiting power with many underlying clusters. They study k-Means and deep grouping under it, introducing Khatri-Rao k-Means and Khatri-Rao deep grouping. Tests show Khatri-Rao k-Means striking a better brevity-accuracy trade-off than k-Means.
arxiv-2603-06802: Moirangthem and colleagues probe loss in superconducting circuits through quasiparticle spectroscopy of tantalum films on sapphire. Microwave tests gauge how well devices work, yet finer probes are needed to grasp why energy leaks and coherence fades at tiny scale. They track Meissner-state magnetism with a precise resonator built for thin films. Samples with poorer quality show extra low-energy excitations. They match deep subgap states from two-level systems, states named for Yu, Shiba, and Rusinov at the gap edge, and perhaps from other pair-breaking causes.
arxiv-2603-07202: Marioriyad and colleagues test language model lying with a set 20-questions game and side-by-side world probing. Lying here means by plan giving false information to serve outside prizes, a risk distinct from chance dreams. At the point of object ID, the chat forks into side-by-side worlds with rival queries. Lying is flagged when a model denies its chosen object across all branches to avoid ID. GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Flash, and Qwen-3-235B are tested across three incentive levels.
arxiv-2603-07302: Bhusal, Alam and Rastogi take a training-centered view of why saliency maps for image classifiers turn out noisy and unstable. They first connect steady explanations with a gently varying gradient field nearby, then show adversarial training trades sharper, steadier maps against output-side wobble. Adding a light Gaussian smoothing block inside the network keeps the sparsity gains while steadying both sides. Human judges rate the smoothed maps as more sufficient and trustworthy.
arxiv-2603-07702: Agarwal and colleagues study single-crystal half-Heusler DyNiSb at low temperatures. Magnetic response, heat capacity and resistivity reveal two magnetic transitions, versus a single shift reported for polycrystals. The crystals conduct like metals, against non-metal results claimed for polycrystal samples. Weak antilocalization appears in small fields and fades with temperature, while angular readings cross from fourfold to twofold symmetry with field strength, hinting at Fermi surface rebuild.
arxiv-2603-08002: Chugg and colleagues develop large-sample procedures that stay valid when significance levels are chosen after seeing data. That is post-hoc valid inference. Classical tools demand that the error level be fixed before any data is seen, so an inconclusive interval cannot be rerun at a larger level. E-values emerged as the necessary and sufficient tool for post-hoc inference, but all such results so far are nonasymptotic. Nonasymptotic tools inherit assumptions and conservatism, while the authors build the asymptotic theory for sharper results under weaker assumptions.
arxiv-2603-08102: Mizoguchi and colleagues construct the E8 lattice from classical error-correcting codes over Mordell-Weil groups of rational elliptic surfaces. They cover every case of Oguiso-Shioda's classification where the singularity lattice has maximal rank 8. By the structure theorem for Mordell-Weil lattices, a maximal singularity rank forces the Mordell-Weil group to be cyclic or a direct sum of cyclic groups. Gluing the singularity lattices together with a code over their natural ring yields the E8 lattice, linking code constructions to this exceptional lattice.
arxiv-2603-08202: Sheludzko and colleagues propose MM-TS, multi-modal temperature and margin schedules for contrastive learning with long-tail data. Contrastive learning pulls positive pairs closer while pushing negatives apart, and in the uni-modal setting temperature controls the strength of those forces. MM-TS extends temperature scheduling to multi-modal learning, adjusting temperature during training to the local mix of each sample. Samples from dense clusters get a higher temperature to preserve their semantic structure. The schedules fit a max-margin framework, unifying InfoNCE and max-margin objectives.
arxiv-2603-08402: He and colleagues propose a cross-device radio frequency fingerprint identification system with channel strength. RFFI exploits own-device hardware flaws for sender ID, but results suffer under device shifts and changing radio channels in cross-device use. In the sign-up stage, a channel-robust prep method constructs cleaned spectral quotient sets, and a DSQ-based CNN is trained on source data. In use, a tuning dataset from both ends feeds a learning network that learns the curved mapping between them.
arxiv-2603-08502: Takayuki Hibi and colleagues define a new class of graphs that mirrors a known kind of ring from algebra. They sort the new graphs with the independence polynomial, which tallies sets of nodes with no links between them by size. The paper gives that sorting for several plain graph families, so readers can see just which members earn the new label.
arxiv-2603-08602: Luca Maggio and Vincenzo Tamma sense the gap between two photons' momenta in three dimensions at once. Their method samples two-photon interference across space and hits the best quantum precision for all three parts together. It needs only about two thousand samples to do so, opening uses in fine 3D positioning, refractometry, and near-field calibration.
arxiv-2603-08702: Daniel Ranard and colleagues show that near-perfect quantum cellular automata in one dimension can always be tidied into exact ones. Approximate rules might in principle behave in wholly new ways, but on a finite circle every near rule rounds to a strict rule with nearly the same local action. The proof works locally, pulling exact boundary algebras from small patches and gluing them into the strict rule.
arxiv-2603-08802: Victor Breso-Pla and colleagues ask whether physics should be built into particle-learning models or learned from data alone. They pit L-GATr against OmniLearn on weakly supervised anomaly detection, likelihood-ratio estimation, and reweight unfolding. Both methods land about even given tuning-data noise, so the gains from encoding known structure look largely method-independent.
arxiv-2603-09002: Tam Nguyen and colleagues score 16 AI safety frameworks against multi-agent system threats. Multi-agent systems wield tools, share memory, and team up across agents, making attack paths old frameworks were not designed for. No reviewed framework covers most of any single group, with chance and data leakage least covered and OWASP's agent drive leading at 65.3 percent score.
arxiv-2603-09402: Kanishka Reddy builds a compact mean-field theory for large networks of coupled phase oscillators that also face quenched randomness. Starting from wrapped Langevin dynamics, a path-integral form keeps the phases' circle nature in view at every step. Averaging over disorder in the large-system limit leaves one stochastic oscillator, driven by a fixed mean field and matched colored Gaussian noise. Without disorder it yields the Ott-Antonsen result and the standard Kuramoto and theta-neuron models.
arxiv-2603-09502: Justyn Snarski-Adamski and colleagues reconcile clashing density functional estimates of magnetocrystalline anisotropy energy, a key trait of permanent magnets. Values shift widely with the chosen potential, clouding the hunt for new magnet materials. Their fully relativistic fixed spin moment method shows each potential's settled pair lies on one shared curve of anisotropy versus spin moment. That curve also bounds the best anisotropy a material could reach and guides alloy choices.
arxiv-2603-09602: Mor Oren-Loberman and colleagues study detecting several hidden submatrices inside a large Gaussian random matrix, where the planted signal varies across entries. Planted entries may deviate by shifted means or inflated variances, each possibly entry-dependent. Placements are either arbitrary or, as in many scientific uses, restricted to consecutive rows and columns. For both signal types and both regimes they prove information-theoretic lower bounds and give algorithms matching them up to logarithmic factors.
arxiv-2603-09702: Fayaz Ali Dharejo and colleagues propose TriFusion-SR, a diffusion system that fuses three medical image types and super-resolves them in one joint step. Splitting the stages breeds artifacts, and tri-modal mixes of anatomical and functional scans suffer strong frequency imbalances. A 2D discrete wavelet transform splits features into frequency bands, letting cross-modal interaction be tuned per band. Rectified wavelet terms calibrate the latent coefficients, and an adaptive fusion module then refines the result across space and frequency.
arxiv-2603-10102: Boyce and Santos work out Kerr black hole ringdown modes within effective field theory, for any spin. Their step by step count gives model free shifts to the ringdown spectrum that wave watchers can test in real data. Near the extreme spin edge, the shifts wobble with the log of a heat ratio tied to the hole. That pattern, they note, points to a hidden scale free structure that repeats at set size steps in the near extreme hole.
arxiv-2603-10202: Alswaidan and Varner fix a double counting flaw in synthetic multi asset equity simulation. A generator fitted to an asset's full returns counts market variance twice once it is reused and a market factor is added. Their fix centres and rescales every draw across a set horizon before the factor is added. Tested on hundreds of United States assets with hidden Markov generators, corrected paths keep heavy tails and recover market loadings well.
arxiv-2603-10602: Omer Friedland and Henrik Ueberschär prove a sharp alternative for eigenfunctions of complex elliptic operators on any open set. Either the zero-free region around such a function has an inner radius bounded below by a set power of the eigenvalue, or something extreme happens instead. In the second case, all of the L2 mass piles into a thin boundary layer of the same small width. The result holds as the eigenvalue grows without bound, for operators of general order with constant coefficients.
arxiv-2603-11002: Tahani Mtar and Radhouane Fekih-Salem model two species in a chemostat. Each species needs the other to grow. They compete for a single nutrient. They face distinct removal rates and mortality. The team maps the model's equilibria and their stability. They then use numerical continuation to draw operating diagrams. These diagrams run over dilution rate and input substrate concentration. Mortality proves decisive. It brings periodic orbits, tri-stability, and codimension-two bifurcations. It lets the partners coexist along stable limit cycles. They coexist there rather than only at equilibria.
arxiv-2603-11202: Pablo Peña and coauthors hunt cold giant planets. They join radial velocities gathered over up to sixteen years with absolute astrometry. The astrometry is from the Hipparcos and Gaia missions. Radial velocity surveys fade at wide separations. Transits rarely catch long periods. Astrometry breaks the inclination degeneracy. It turns minimum masses into true masses. Extending a Chilean survey of metal-rich stars, they characterize two known planets. They detect five new ones. Astrometry shrinks period and mass uncertainties several-fold. It sharply raises detection confidence.
arxiv-2603-11302: Monica Motta, Michele Palladino, and Franco Rampazzo tackle a mismatch between two routes to necessary conditions in optimal control problems with a target. Set separation and penalization give non-equivalent results. The clash traces to notions of tangency at the target. They show the Clarke tangent cone serves as a quasi differential quotient approximating cone under local invariance or prox-regularity. For impulsive control, the result links infimum gaps for minimizers to higher abnormality. That abnormality sits in a maximum principle built on Lie brackets.
arxiv-2603-11402: Esmailpour and Sintos tackle a cost problem in work on relational data. Joins expose the full data set, yet building them can be far too slow for tasks like clustering. Their fix is the RBBD tree, a randomized form of the BBD tree made for database settings. Sampling and counting over joins let the tree grow only where it is needed. The payoff is clustering for k-center, k-means, and k-median that runs faster by a factor of k, with the same quality guarantees.
arxiv-2603-12002: Hindes, Prasad, McGuire, and Schwartz study what happens when two swarms move through each other. Each swarm holds its own stable preferred velocity before the two groups meet. The authors build a framework for the collision and test it with a rigid-body approximation. Redirection after impact occurs when the merged system has a stable synchronized state. Scaling rules from the model match both particle simulations and runs with wheeled robots, across matched and opposed settings.
arxiv-2603-12202: Dinga and co-authors design carbon-neutral district heating for homes without straining the power grid. District heating can cut heat emissions fast, yet design must weigh cost, public acceptance, and grid load together. Their method pairs power flow simulation with a modeling-to-generate-alternatives search for planners. A Dutch case shows wide diversity in how such networks can be built. Smart placement of heat pumps and thermal storage limits grid stress. High electrification levels prove possible even when green heat sources run scarce.
arxiv-2603-12502: Watanabe and co-authors study ferroaxial magnets, a fresh class of magnets driven by spin order. In them, magnetic order breaks mirror symmetry while time reversal and spatial inversion stay intact. The axial anisotropy that results allows optical control of the ferroaxial polarization. Spin group analysis then picks out candidate hosts. Some hosts pair the order with metallic conductivity, forming a ferroaxial metal. The team proposes a third-order Hall effect as a direct probe of that metal. The work opens a fresh route for spin-based devices.
arxiv-2603-12902: Florian Ecker's thesis explores Carroll symmetries across field theory and gravity, starting from the geometry of curved Carroll manifolds. On such backgrounds, scalar and vector Carroll swiftons are studied. Causality and locality yield a universal sector for stress-energy commutators in any Carroll quantum theory. In two dimensions, a boost anomaly adds Schwinger-like terms tied to flat gravity symmetries. The thesis then builds Carroll gravity models, with black holes that carry an extremal surface, not a horizon. A Carroll-Hawking effect appears for the Carroll-Schwarzschild case.
arxiv-2603-13202: J. Hlinka revisits neutron scattering data on PMN, the canonical relaxor ferroelectric perovskite oxide. The aim is to gauge the role of intrinsic bulk flexoelectricity in this material. The flexoelectric coupling value drawn from the diffuse scattering data stays in a familiar range. It does not exceed values seen in conventional perovskite ferroelectrics. Hlinka links this result to Ginzburg-Landau-Devonshire theory and soft mode theory. He suggests relaxor traits may stem from a shortened transverse correlation length near the Lifshitz-point regime.
arxiv-2603-13402: Chika Maduabuchi and Jindong Wang present Event-Driven Video Generation for text-to-video models. Such models can make frames look right yet botch simple interactions, like motion before contact. Frame-first denoising updates every latent region at each step, even where no interaction should occur. Their EVD add-on gives the sampler an explicit event signal through a lightweight head. Event-gated sampling applies updates mainly where an interaction forms. On EVD-Bench it raised human preference and dynamics scores while keeping appearance quality.
arxiv-2603-13502: Wenchao Wu and co-authors study safety-aware goal-oriented semantic sensing, communication, and control for robotics. Wireless links to edge servers can flood with data, adding latency that degrades robot tasks. Goal-oriented semantic communication sends only goal-relevant data, but it often overlooks safety needs. The authors propose a co-design that treats safety across sensing, communication, and control as one closed loop. They set out an architecture, use cases, and safety requirements. A UAV tracking case study more than doubled safety and success rates.
arxiv-2603-13702: Dongyuan Li and co-authors propose xCPD, a plugin for routing channel-patch dependencies in time series forecasting. Channel-Independent modeling treats each channel alone, which can miss inter-channel interactions and generalize poorly. Channel-Dependent modeling pools all channels, which can add irrelevant data and oversmooth. The plugin projects multivariate signals into the frequency domain with a shared graph Fourier basis. Patches are grouped into low-, mid-, and high-frequency bands by spectral energy. A channel-adaptive routing mechanism then sets inter-channel interaction per patch.
arxiv-2603-13902: Virovlyansky analyzes broadband sound pulses recorded by a vertical array in Lake Kinneret, Israel. At most pulse frequencies the array is sparse, which limits direct reading of the field. An autoproduct transform rebuilds the signals as if sent at low frequencies, where the array is dense. The field is then mapped into a depth-angle-time space, where it proves stable against environmental change. The map matches an idealized waveguide model and can feed a neural network that locates sound sources.
arxiv-2603-14002: Feghhi and co-authors present LightBeam, a decoder that turns brain signals into text for speech neuroprostheses. The standard decoder for this task needs about 320 GB of memory, which shuts out many users and labs. LightBeam needs only about 10 GB and drops the old WFST design. It folds a language model into beam search with delayed fusion, so no large n-gram model is needed. On the Brain-to-Text '24 and '25 benchmarks, it matches the best reported results.
arxiv-2603-14302: Wu studies partition functions for time-inhomogeneous branching random walks with shrinking variance steps. The model links to two-dimensional directed polymers. By reworking Berestycki's Gaussian multiplicative chaos framework to drop its martingale needs, the author proves key facts. The critical value matches the time-homogeneous case, and partition functions converge in the subcritical regime. The same decay rate holds at criticality too. Open problems on chaos beyond log-correlated fields close the work.
arxiv-2603-14702: Zhang, Kang and Lu estimate depth from one image with a fractal autoregressive diffusion design. Autoregressive generation suits depth poorly in raw form. Pixel-wise steps waste compute, and discrete tokens jar with smooth depth values. Their method builds depth scale by scale, coarse to fine. A fusion module blends image features with the current depth guess. A diffusion loss models depth in continuous space directly. Reused generator units form a fractal stack for speed. A consensus step merges samples and flags unsure pixels.
arxiv-2603-14802: Williams and co-authors ship OpenReservoirComputing, a JAX library for reservoir computing on GPUs. Reservoir methods lift a signal into a high-dimensional dynamical system. Only a simple linear readout needs training. Chaotic time-series forecasting is the flagship use case. The library builds on JAX and the Equinox framework. Just-in-time compilation, automatic vectorization and GPU speed come built in. Modular parts support custom models, with stock models for forecasting, classification and control. Bigger reservoirs and faster prototyping are the design goals.
arxiv-2603-15102: Ohkuma and co-authors probe superconductivity in Bi-2223 crystals under high pressure with quantum microscopy. The microscope uses nitrogen-vacancy centers to image the Meissner response over a wide field. Earlier studies disagreed on how the transition temperature moves with pressure, partly due to different pressure media. The team compares cBN and KBr media directly. In KBr, a diamagnetic signal near 70 K lasted up to 23 gigapascals. In cBN it vanished above 11 gigapascals, showing how strongly the pressure environment matters.
arxiv-2603-15402: Wang and co-authors probe how large language models understand tables, testing sixteen models across general, tabular, and mixture-of-experts types. They track attention flow, layer depth, expert use, and input design. Attention moves in three phases: early layers scan wide, middle layers find key cells, late layers boost them. Table tasks need deeper layers than math tasks before predictions settle. Mixture models route to table experts in the middle layers. Chain-of-thought prompts raise table attention, and table tuning raises it further.
arxiv-2603-15602: Cocconi, Mahault, and Piro model a tiny self-steering particle that senses its surroundings. Smart active agents must split a finite energy budget across sensing, steering, and motion. The model tracks a polarity-cue sensor linked to an outside field. It splits entropy production into locomotion, actuation, and sensing costs. Pareto fronts link energy spent to accuracy in localization and path following. The results show that clear thermodynamic bounds limit feedback-controlled motion.
arxiv-2603-15702: Leplat, O'Callaghan, and Bankhead connect the QuPath image tool to OMERO servers. QuPath is free software for viewing and scoring large microscopy images. Local-only storage limits its use in big studies. Their new extension pulls pixels and metadata straight from OMERO. Labs can then work on remotely stored image sets with ease. The extension also serves as a template for other links. Developers can copy the pattern to reach other image stores.
arxiv-2603-15802: Potapczynski and co-authors teach a forecaster to use outside signals, not just history. Retail demand, power load, and prices all swing with outside drivers. Most foundation forecasters ignore those covariates and read history alone. Their ApolloPFN is a prior-fitted network with time awareness built in. A synthetic prior injects trends, breaks, and covariate links. Time-aware layers add the context biases the task needs. Tests on M5, power prices, air quality, and solar data beat prior baselines.
arxiv-2603-15902: Bar and Wells add random effects to the SEMMS variable picker. SEMMS selects markers in generalized linear models with a mixture prior. Its base form treats all observations as independent. Clustered and repeated data break that premise in practice. Ignoring within-subject links inflates noise and spoils selection. Their extension adds random intercepts, slopes, or both. A coordinate-ascent loop updates subject predictors with lmer or glmer fits. Fixed-effect picks then run on the adjusted response. Hard cases recover the true set far more often.
arxiv-2603-16202: Liu and Zhu tackle crowding at electric vehicle charging stations. Cars charge slowly, so demand spikes can clog a station. Their plan works in two stages. First, a coordinator sets entry quotas per station to cap the worst delay. Next, cars are assigned to stations to raise total utility. A participation model then shows when drivers will join. Tests show much lower worst-case crowding with small utility loss.
arxiv-2603-16402: Gomez models black holes sitting inside dark matter halos. No single accepted method exists for building such spacetimes. His perturbative approach deforms a round black hole step by step. He computes first corrections to the photon sphere and shadow size. The formulas assume a generic halo profile. Two named profiles, Hernquist and Navarro-Frenk-White, give closed forms. Shadow shifts fall far below current telescope bounds. The enclosed dark matter mass also stays under the GRAVITY limit.
arxiv-2603-16502: Carmans, Petrov, and Nesladek read out a diamond NV qubit's state with electric current. NV centers are strong room-temperature qubit candidates. Their spin is usually read by light emission. Optical readout needs microscope resolution, which blocks dense spin layouts. The team instead performs quantum state tomography with photoelectric readout. State fidelity reached 0.995, matching parallel optical measures. Photocurrent delays slow the method, and a model explains them.
arxiv-2603-16702: Fang simulates how nuclear recoils ionize semiconductor detectors at ultra-low energies. That yield is a key uncertainty for dark matter and neutrino experiments. His molecular dynamics method skips fitted parameters entirely. Crystal effects enter the transport directly, from high energies down to one electron-hole pair. The model matches silicon data best to date, sharpest at that lowest level. Yields come out as full distributions, not single values. The spread extends dark matter limits to lighter masses. Germanium modeling adds quantum and channeling effects.
arxiv-2603-16902: Montambaux revisits Lord Kelvin's famous 1900 speech about two clouds over physics. Kelvin gave the speech at the Royal Institution on April 27, 1900. The second cloud is often said to concern black body radiation. Montambaux argues it really concerned the specific heat of polyatomic molecules. He places the speech in its historical sequence, from Kirchhoff to the first Solvay Conference in 1911. He also shows that Planck's first motive was not the so called ultraviolet catastrophe. The article corrects a common story about the birth of quantum mechanics.
arxiv-2603-17002: Sánchez-Martínez and co-authors study acoustic plasmons, nicknamed demons, in multiband metals. These are gapless charge waves from electrons in different bands moving out of phase. The team uses a hydrodynamic model for high temperatures and a microscopic model for low ones. Once disorder is included, the mode frequency turns purely imaginary. The wave then spreads diffusively over a range of small wave vectors. They say this explains the anomalous dispersion reported for the demon in Sr2RuO4.
arxiv-2603-17102: Bandarkar, Ansell, and Cohn use cross lingual inconsistency to locate knowledge inside mixture of experts language models. Models often recall a fact in one language but fail in another. Their framework contrasts expert routing for languages where recall succeeds against languages where it fails. A statistical test on router logits then names the experts that matter for that fact. To validate, they switch those experts off and ask again. Turning off about 20 of roughly 6,000 experts made the model fail over 40 percent of previously correct answers.
arxiv-2603-17202: Qiu and co-authors study linear quadratic Gaussian games where agents must estimate the state with sparse shared observations. Standard setups assume every agent uses all observations at hand, which is unrealistic in large systems. Their distributed estimator weighs accuracy against sparsity through a group lasso problem. Agents then play feedback Nash strategies based on their estimates. The authors give rules that guarantee a corrective reset to the best estimation gain. In formation game simulations, communication use fell a lot.
arxiv-2603-17502: Healy and co-authors present a light framework for extreme rainfall risk in climate ensembles. Their entry tackles the EVA 2025 Data Challenge on exceedance odds at several sites. They skip full spatial dependence and work with spatial order statistics instead. Peaks-over-threshold models with generalized Pareto tails handle the extremes. Month-driven additive models let parameters drift over the year. A conditional model covers back-to-back extremes at one site.
arxiv-2603-17702: Tang and co-authors design a training-free semantic communication scheme with caching. End-to-end learned codecs cost heavy training and adapt poorly to changing channels. Their CAGI-JSCC method inverts a pre-trained GAN while baking channel traits into the process. A shared cache stores split semantic parts at both ends for reuse. Repeat content then skips the air entirely. Image tests matched quality at a bandwidth ratio of 1/224, they report.
arxiv-2603-17902: Yang and Zhu study privacy leaks from enterprise data inside AI agent replies. Most guard work watches user prompts, not the company data behind answers. Their frame treats reply generation as a random map from prompts and datasets to text. Token-level and message-level differential privacy bounds follow from that view. Leak size ties to settings like temperature and reply length, they show. A design problem then picks the best temperature trade-off.
arxiv-2603-18002: Qu and co-authors present Loc3R-VLM, a framework that gives vision-language models real 3D skill from mono video. Two joint goals drive it: rebuild the global layout and model the viewer's own situation. Light camera pose priors from a 3D base model keep scale and geometry in line. It leads on language-based localization in their tests. It also beats 2D and video rivals on situated and general 3D question answering.
arxiv-2603-18202: Morihira and co-authors propose R2-Dreamer, a decoder-free world model for image-based reinforcement learning. Reconstruction methods waste capacity on large task-irrelevant image regions. Decoder-free rivals lean on data augmentation, which limits their range. R2-Dreamer uses a Barlow Twins style redundancy cut as an internal regularizer against collapse. On DeepMind Control and Meta-World it matches DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2, trains 1.59 times faster than DreamerV3, and gains on tiny-object tasks.
arxiv-2603-18702: Tanaka and co-authors tackle off-policy learning when items come in limited supply. Standard methods assume a policy can pick the same item endlessly. Coupons and stock limits break that assumption. A greedy pick for the current user can drain stock that later users would value more. Theory shows greedy methods can fail to maximize returns here. Their OPLS method favors users whose gain beats what other users would get. Tests on synthetic and real data show OPLS ahead of prior methods under supply limits.
arxiv-2603-18802: Hoshi and Iida count simplest cubic fields with small class numbers. Each field comes from a cubic polynomial set by one integer parameter m. Computations with PARI/GP sort fields by the index of a natural order. For index one, 581 values of m give class number at most 1000. Index three and 27 give 80 and 142 such values. Up to ten million, only 138 values keep the class number below 16. The authors list all of them with certified class groups. They conjecture the 26 class-number-one cases are complete.
arxiv-2603-18902: Ennayar and Hussong present a two-color laser method for watching drops hit thin liquid films. The method maps film depth and dye spread at the same time, in space and time. They test water drops across varied flow and impact settings. A spread measure shows how even the mix becomes. It marks the shift from impact-driven flow to slow diffusion mixing. They give a formula for that shift and show the method also works for alcohol-water films.
arxiv-2603-19302: Hou and co-authors erase one class of behavior from a clinical language model by editing very few weights. Their STEU method picks key tokens by a mutual information score. Only those token embeddings and a small classifier head are updated. All deeper encoder layers stay frozen. On MIMIC and eICU data, the target class is nearly wiped out. In the main test, forget F1 falls to 0.0004 while kept-task scores stay sound. Just 0.19 percent of weights are changed.
arxiv-2603-19502: Farhana and co-authors improve separation trade-offs for unlabeled multi-robot motion planning. Unit-disk robots move in a polygonal space, and any robot may take any target. Fast algorithms exist only when starts, targets, and obstacles stay well apart. The team gives polynomial-time constant-approximation algorithms at much tighter spacing. Some plans are monotone, others weakly so, with matching lower bounds on spacing. A near-optimal plan at robot spacing 2 costs a linear approximation factor.
arxiv-2603-19802: Teuber and co-authors test whether vision foundation models help microscopy image classification. Interactive pixel and object classification still often uses shallow feature-based tools. Data diversity and label costs keep deep learning at bay here. The team paired several foundation models with shallow learning and attentive probing. The model set spans SAM variants, DINOv3, and domain-specific tools. Five diverse datasets served as the test bed. The foundation models beat hand-crafted features across the board. The study also sets a benchmark for future microscopy tools.
arxiv-2603-19902: Alessandrelli and co-authors propose a federated way to train associative memory networks. Federated learning trains across clients without sharing raw data, but mixed data and drift can break it. Each client turns its data into a low-rank Hebbian operator and sends that to a server. The server merges these into shared global archetypes. The team frames merging as a spectral inference problem and derives detection limits. An entropy controller balances stability and new learning. Tests with drift and novelty show better archetype recovery.
arxiv-2603-20202: Al-Kharsan, Sahandi, and Shirmohammadi study rings graded by a cancellation monoid through their graded modules. To judge when such rings are hereditary or semihereditary, the basic module tools need graded forms. The authors revisit graded free, projective, injective, and flat modules. They prove graded versions of Baer's criterion for injectivity and Lazard's theorem on flatness. With that base, they characterize graded left hereditary and semihereditary rings. Special attention goes to graded-Prüfer and graded-Dedekind domains. The work extends classic ring theory into the monoid-graded setting.
arxiv-2603-20302: Kaygorodov and Uzakbaev build a new family of algebras from the algebra of polynomials. Their method uses derivation and integration steps set out by Dzhumadildaev. They study basic traits of these integro-derivation algebras. One result is a new class of simple conservative algebras with no finite dimension. They also work out the derivations of these algebras at ranks one and two. The work adds to what is known about algebras formed in this way.
arxiv-2603-20602: Dong and co-authors propose SC-Net, a spectral method for hard inverse problems. Noise makes such problems unstable, so they need strong regularization. SC-Net works in the spectrum of the forward operator. It learns a filter that weights each part by signal to noise ratio. They prove it tracks the true inverse operator at any grid size. On 1D integral tests it hit the best known convergence rate. It also beat oracle Tikhonov filters and held up on finer grids.
arxiv-2603-20802: Beran and co-authors link bounds on curvature to whether a spacetime can be extended further. Their key tool is synthetic curvature, a notion that works at low regularity. They tie curvature bounds to the causal type of length maximizing curves. This bridge lets them relate inextendibility to curvature that grows without bound. Older methods from classical geometry cannot reach that link. The result strengthens a 2019 theorem of Grant, Kunzinger, and Sämann. It also adds a new route to questions about spacetime ends.
arxiv-2603-21102: Luo and co-authors propose evidential quantum vertical federated learning. In vertical federated learning, parties hold different features of the same samples, and must learn together without sharing raw data. Their hybrid classical and quantum design maps each party's features into a quantum state. The states go to the server by quantum teleportation. An evidential fusion circuit then merges them for inference. On image and other real data sets, the method beats classical and quantum baselines at similar parameter budgets.
arxiv-2603-21202: Kapusta and co-authors report the first observation of a lineshape asymmetry shift in a short-baseline atomic gravimeter. The shift comes from asymmetry in the interferometer lineshape. It falls with the cube of the free evolution time. At millisecond scale evolution times, it can bias the measured value of gravity by a tenth to one milligal. That is a real concern for compact, high precision gravimeters. The measurements agree well with the team's earlier theoretical studies. They stress that the shift must be counted in absolute gravity measurements.
arxiv-2603-21502: Dong and Cheng study shallow neural networks through the geometry of their parameter symmetries. Many parameter choices give the same predictor, thanks to hidden-unit swaps and rescalings. Curvature measured in raw parameter space can thus reflect the representation, not the predictor itself. They build a quotient space that mods out the symmetries and define curvature there. Gradient flow splits into a part that moves the predictor and a pure gauge part. Experiments back the claim that quotient curvature organizes local dynamics better.
arxiv-2603-21702: Bresciani and co-authors introduce neutral representations of finite groups and group schemes. A representation counts as neutral when any twisted form of the classifying stack that carries a matching vector bundle must itself be neutral. In plain terms, the bundle's existence forces the gerbe to have a rational point. They give criteria for representations of finite diagonalizable group schemes to be neutral. Applying the idea, they produce wide families of curves and pointed varieties with cyclic automorphism groups that are defined over their field of moduli.
arxiv-2603-21902: Shen and Zhuge study boundary behavior for elliptic equations with periodic coefficients at a tiny scale, with no smoothness assumed on the coefficients. Classic tools measure solutions at the boundary, but rough coefficients force a change. They define large-scale maximal functions that probe solutions one period away from the boundary. For the Dirichlet, Neumann, and regularity problems, they prove L^p bounds that do not depend on the small scale. The ranges of p match the optimal ones for the Laplace operator. Extra smoothness restores the classic results.
arxiv-2603-22002: Nguyen and Tran-Truong present SegMaFormer, a hybrid model for 3D medical image segmentation. The model mixes Mamba state-space layers with Transformer attention in one encoder. Mamba layers run first, at high resolution, to keep costs low. Attention runs later, at low resolution, to refine the features. The authors also add rotary position embeddings for spatial awareness. They report Dice scores on Synapse, BraTS, and ACDC that match much larger models. The model uses up to 75 times fewer parameters and far fewer FLOPs.
arxiv-2603-22302: Wei and co-authors cluster college students by traits to guide career advice. Most past work predicts career paths, not trait fit. The team studies data on more than 3,000 students. The data covers CET-4 scores, grades, personality traits, and student cadre experience. A K-means algorithm sorts the students into four groups with like traits. Each group then gets career guidance matched to its profile. The authors report that trait mixes suit different career paths. They argue the grouping gives a sound base for personal guidance.
arxiv-2603-22502: Zachariah and co-authors present MapForest, a field robotics system that maps forests and locates invasive trees. Crews now scout by hand, and satellite signals fade under the canopy. MapForest pairs a portable sensor payload with LiDAR-inertial mapping and image-based species detection. The payload mounts on a drone, a bicycle, or a backpack. The team trained a detector for tree-of-heaven and tested the system across six sites. Drift stayed under two meters on a long forest run, and maps come out GIS-ready.
arxiv-2603-22702: Fei starts a new line of work: testing traits of distributions over graph edges. Such tests matter for a free-form style of graph property testing. Fei proves near-tight sample bounds for three traits. Testing bipartiteness needs on the order of n samples. Triangle-freeness needs about n to the four-thirds power. Square-freeness needs about n to the nine-eighths power. The square-free proof uses new birthday-paradox style lemmas. Fei also links the results to Turán problems and subgraph removal lemmas.
arxiv-2603-22802: Garg presents new results on finite-time and fixed-time convergence for dynamical systems. He uses LaSalle-like invariance ideas to relax standard demands. His Lyapunov-like results allow non-smooth functions, with no need for a smooth, positive definite Lyapunov function. Both first- and second-order versions are given. Garg then shows a key link: any system with a globally stable equilibrium can be rescaled. The rescaled system gains a fixed-time stable equilibrium. The work supports the view that convergence rates connect through the right transform.
arxiv-2603-23402: Datta and eight co-authors compare niobium films for superconducting qubits grown at different temperatures. Three epitaxial films grew on sapphire under near-identical conditions. The team pairs magneto-optical imaging of flux patterns with penetration depth readings. The low-quality film screens fields weakly and shows an irregular depth curve. That points to localized in-gap states inside it. High-quality films show the opposite pattern. The authors offer the paired tests as a fast route to screen films. Better screening should lift quantum circuit performance.
arxiv-2603-23602: Baldwin shows that quantum annealing shines at near-miss optimization in spin glasses. Annealing is prized for ground states, but low states that fall just short matter too. Mean field p-spin models were long thought to trap all dynamics at one threshold energy. Recent work showed two stage quenches can slip below that line. Baldwin proves quantum annealing does the same trick in constant time. Its leftover energy falls with a decay exponent up to twice the classical one.
arxiv-2603-23702: Cassar and ten co-authors compute B-meson decay form factors on the lattice. Their grids use the improved staggered quark action for sea and valence quarks alike. Runs span four lattice spacings, many at true pion masses. On the finest grids, the b quark sits at its real mass. The team detail their two- and three-point correlation work. Early chiral-continuum fits give scalar and vector factors for B to D type decays. Percent-level factors would sharpen key CKM elements.
arxiv-2603-23802: Stein counts how AI agents are used in practice, based on 177,436 tools built for the Model Context Protocol. The tools span November 2024 to February 2026. Stein sorts them into tools that read data, tools that reason, and tools that act on the world. Software work makes up 67 percent of tools and 90 percent of server downloads. The share of action tools rose from 27 to 65 percent of use. Stein shows how regulators could watch risks at the tool layer.
arxiv-2603-24102: Zhou and co-authors build a theory of electron transport driven by surface acoustic waves. Past work treated such waves as plain electric fields, missing how they fold the Brillouin zone. Their semiclassical framework treats the wave as a quasi-periodic potential that reshapes electron momentum. It explains the observed DC drag current and predicts an acousto-electric Hall effect. It also predicts anomalous Hall, thermal Hall, and Nernst effects in time-reversal symmetric systems. Worked examples use bilayer graphene and MX2 materials.
arxiv-2603-24202: Sancaktar and co-authors study how to scale reinforcement learning for code generation with synthetic data. A teacher model refines problems over several turns, guided by summaries of student performance. This multi-turn pipeline yields more valid problems than single-turn generation. It also creates easier and harder variants of one task, which form natural curricula. Tests span Llama and Qwen model families. Synthetic data improve code scores and often math scores too. The authors map how difficulty, scheduling, and diversity shape training.
arxiv-2603-24402: Long presents AI-Supervisor, a multi-agent framework that oversees AI research from literature review to paper writing. Most automated research tools run as stateless pipelines with no lasting grasp of the field. This system keeps a Research World Model, a knowledge graph of methods, benchmarks, limits, and open gaps, shared by all agents. Agents find gaps by breaking methods into modules, probe why modules fail, and borrow fixes from other fields. A consensus mechanism lets agents check and challenge each other's findings.
arxiv-2603-24502: Gao and co-authors find a new source of purely finite matricial fields. A group is matricial field if matrices can mimic its regular representation under strong convergence, with stricter variants. With a new operator algebraic approach, they study amalgamated free products built over a separable subgroup. When one side is exact, the product of a matricial field group with a residually finite one keeps the same property.
